scoreNote: Strong-adequate (4.5): a two-view response that leans toward funding the arts while granting the risk to integrity; two developed examples with analysis, controlled prose on a memorable First and Second skeleton.

sentences.text: Without money, many artists and theatres could not survive, yet money can also bring control.
Some believe government funding of the arts is necessary so the arts can flourish for all, while others believe such funding threatens the integrity of the arts.
I lean toward the view that funding is necessary, but I accept that it can endanger artistic integrity.

sections.role: Body 1 — Why funding helps the arts flourish

sentences.text: First, government funding genuinely helps the arts flourish and reach everyone.
Many valuable works of art could never be made without public support.
For example, free museums and funded theatres let poor families enjoy art they could not otherwise afford.
This shows that public funding can make the arts available to all, not just the rich.
Support also lets artists take creative risks instead of chasing only what sells.
Without funding, much important culture would simply disappear.
For these reasons, I believe government support for the arts is necessary.

sections.role: Body 2 — Why funding can threaten integrity

sentences.text: Second, however, the opposing view rightly warns that funding can threaten artistic integrity.
A government that pays for art may try to control what artists are allowed to say.
Consider an artist who softens her honest message for fear of losing her public funding.
Such pressure shows that money can quietly limit the freedom art depends on.
Funding may also favour safe, official art over bold or critical work.
Art that must please the government can lose the honesty that gives it real value.
Both views, then, capture a real truth about funding the arts.
In conclusion, I believe government funding is necessary for the arts to flourish and reach all people.
But it can threaten artistic integrity, so it must be given with care.
The wisest funding supports the arts generously while protecting the freedom that keeps them honest.
